summary: Guided rollback request: mixed optimizer profiles + per-tenant KV prefetch causing intermittent tail latency and OOMs
description: Customer BrightNote Health reports intermittent high tail latency (95th/99th spikes) and occasional worker OOMs starting after a recent optimizer rollout. The rollout included tenant-scoped KV prefetch settings and per-tenant quantization profiles. Multiple tenants show divergent behavior: some have improved throughput while others (notably clinical inference routes) experience long stalls and retries. Customer requests a guided safe rollback to baseline and verification steps before re-enabling any optimizer variants.
impact: Production inference for clinical routes affected. Increased 95th/99th latency causing degraded user experience and several failed requests. Some worker pods restarted due to OOM resulting in short unavailability windows. Customer is enterprise and requires an SLA-aware recovery path.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Using BrightNote prod cluster (us-east-1) with tenant IDs TN-1003 and TN-1021, send mixed-length chat requests with max tokens ~1024.
2) Ensure optimizer flags are set: kv_prefetch_enabled=true for TN-1003, per_tenant_quant_profile=aggressive for TN-1021.
3) Observe token-level tail latency in Console traces and increased OOM events in worker logs.
4) Disable one of the optimizer features and compare latency/eviction rates.
logs: Pod logs (cluster/prod/us-east-1): worker-7f9b OOMKilled at 2026-03-09T23:02Z, stack: runtime::kv_cache::evict()
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: aggressive per-tenant quant profile increases memory working set; combined with kv_prefetch we exceed cache budget causing evictions and longer KV fetch paths.
Observed correlation between tenant-specific optimizer flags and which model variant served (quantized vs FP16).
Console checks: token cache hit rate dropped from 78% to 43% for TN-1021 after rollout; TN-1003 shows increased synchronous KV fetch latency.

resolution: In progress - baseline restore applied to critical tenant TN-1021 and KV cache flushed; monitoring shows reduced tail latency. Full rollback plan for all affected tenants scheduled. Final validation pending 24h stability window.
remediation_plan: 1) Freeze current optimizer flags and take system snapshot via Console (configs/snapshot create).
2) For highest-impact tenants (list provided to customer), revert per-tenant quant profile to 'baseline' and disable kv_prefetch via API: PATCH /v1/tenants/{id}/config.
3) Flush tenant KV caches: POST /v1/cache/flush?tenant_id=... (staged, one tenant at a time).
4) Roll pods using rolling restart with maxUnavailable=1 to avoid capacity shock.
5) Monitor 95th/99th latency, worker RSS, and eviction rates for 2x baseline observation windows before re-enabling any optimizer flag.
6) If metrics regress, re-apply conservative config: per-tenant batching capped at 8, quant_profile=balanced, prefetch=false.
7) Create follow-up ticket for gradual re-introduction with canary at 1% of traffic and A/B evaluation.
follow_up_actions: Document tenant-scoped rollback notes in Confluence page linked above.
Add automated preflight checks to the optimizer rollout pipeline: memory working set forecast and per-tenant cache budget checks.
Schedule a joint postmortem with customer and runtime team to define safer rollout constraints.
